assumptions: Both arms curl together and symmetrically, so the exercise is bilateral.
The neutral (palms-in) grip is held throughout with no forearm pronation or supination, so no radioulnar action is listed.
The torso stays stationary, so there is no trunk or hip action; standing posture is covered by postural stabilization.
The load is held in the hands on the rope, so grip and wrist stability apply.
Reps are the input mode, as is usual for curls.
Joint actions describe the concentric curl phase, and the cable path is treated as the resistance direction.
classification_reasons: Standing bilateral cable hammer curl with a rope on a low pulley; the instructions and both frames agree on elbows pinned at the sides, a neutral grip, and only the forearms moving.
The movement fits the vocabulary: elbow flexion is the prime action, with a neutral-grip hold and the upper arm held still.
